subject: Modified CFI in measurement invariance models (Lai & Yoon, 2014)

messages.author: 6c4d187713e325b8
messages.subject: Modified CFI in measurement invariance models (Lai & Yoon, 2014)
parts:
Hi All,

        I was wondering if it were possible to run measurementinvariance() using the modified CFI proposed by Lai & Yoon (2015). They demonstrated substancial difficulties using delta CFI for establishing measurement invariance due to variations in baseline models. As a result, their alternative CFI appears to correct this error. 


Mark H. C. Lai & Myeongsun Yoon (2015) A Modified Comparative Fit Index for Factorial Invariance Studies, Structural Equation Modeling: A Multidisciplinary Journal, 22:2, 236-248, DOI: 10.1080/10705511.2014.935928


Kind Regards,
          Conal Monaghan

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Modified CFI in measurement invariance models (Lai & Yoon, 2014)
parts: their alternative CFI appears to correct this error.

Well, it doesn't correct anything, it is just the same concept of incremental fit applied relative to different models, perhaps more relevant to evaluating (not testing) invariance.  So instead of putting your model on a continuum somewhere between saturation and independence, you define the ends of the continuum as the most restrictive measurement model and the least restrictive (i.e., configural).  I think it's a cool idea, but it is not implemented in semTools (yet).  I doubt it would be out in the next version, unless someone else can come up with a general way to automatically specify that special constrained model based on the configural model syntax.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
